channel.title: Frontier Wire
channel.description: AI news: frontier labs, research, policy and commentary.

item.title: SAP prepares plan to eliminate at least 10,000 positions for AI shift
item.description: SAP is preparing a plan to eliminate at least 10,000 positions, or 9% of its global staff. The restructuring aims to transform its software business for the artificial intelligence era. The restructuring highlights how major enterprise software providers are shifting capital and human resources away from traditional operations to prioritize artificial intelligence.

item.title: Avicena raises $100M+ Series C for microLED optical interconnects
item.description: Avicena raised over $100 million in a Series C funding round led by Intervest to commercialize its microLED-based optical interconnect technology for AI infrastructure. The funding included participation from corporate venture arms such as SK Hynix, Samsung, and AMD. As copper links and traditional lasers face physical limits in AI data centers, chipmakers are investing in alternative optical technologies to overcome data bottlenecks between processors and memory.

item.title: Chariot AI unveils Chariot-1 LLM and speech models under IndiaAI Mission
item.description: Chariot AI has launched the Chariot-1 model suite under the IndiaAI Mission, featuring an 11-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts language model and a text-to-speech system supporting 10 Indian languages. The models were pre-trained from scratch in India and incorporate research innovations designed to improve computational efficiency and reduce token usage. The release highlights government-backed efforts to build sovereign foundation models tailored to Indian scripts, addressing the high token costs and inefficiencies that standard English-centric models face in multilingual environments.

item.title: Texas resumes data center permitting and approves SpaceX gas plant
item.description: Texas resumed data center permitting by approving permits for SpaceX's $24 billion gas power plant. The approval occurred ahead of Democratic Governor Gina Hinojosa taking office in January. The rapid approval ahead of a change in political leadership highlights how companies are rushing to secure infrastructure permits before incoming administrations implement stricter oversight.

item.title: Netherlands seeks to block US MATCH Act restricting ASML China sales
item.description: The Dutch government announced it will resist the US proposed MATCH Act, which aims to restrict ASML Holding NV's sales and maintenance services in China. Dutch Foreign Minister Tom Berendsen stated that the Netherlands intends to prevent the bill from becoming law, calling the proposal a threat to Europe's most valuable company. The dispute pits a key American ally against US lawmakers attempting to include the export control measure in the fiscal year 2027 National Defense Authorization Act.

item.title: ASML CEO warns aggressive export controls will push China to build domestic tech
item.description: ASML CEO Christophe Fouquet argued that export controls should not completely cut off China, warning that such a strategy would backfire by accelerating domestic development. ASML holds a $520 billion de facto monopoly in making lithography machines for advanced AI chips. The debate highlights tensions between protecting advanced technology and maintaining market share, as ASML currently supplies China with equipment that is over a decade behind the cutting edge.

item.title: Z.ai misses GLM-5.5 launch as US rules and distillation curbs hit China AI
item.description: Z.ai missed the scheduled November release for its 3-trillion-parameter flagship model, GLM-5.5, due to US computing restrictions and anti-distillation measures. Rival Moonshot AI also warns that losing access to overseas computing power could double the interval between its major releases. These restrictions threaten the cost-advantage model that has allowed Chinese AI developers to compete globally despite ongoing hardware export controls.

item.title: Thariq Shihipar joins OpenAI after leaving Anthropic
item.description: Thariq Shihipar has joined OpenAI following his departure from Anthropic in October. Shihipar previously worked as a Member of Technical Staff on Anthropic's Claude Code team. The departure of a prominent public-facing engineer from Anthropic's Claude Code team to OpenAI illustrates the ongoing interchange of technical personnel between leading AI developers.

item.title: AI labs may hold unreleased breakthroughs that could break current cryptosystems
item.description: Computer scientist Scott Aaronson said leading AI labs likely possess major, unreleased algorithmic breakthroughs that could break deployed cryptosystems, though the exact nature of the breakthroughs is unknown. If the breakthroughs can undermine existing encryption, data security and financial systems that rely on current cryptography could be at risk.

item.title: SoftBank default risk hits 4-year high amid AI investment worries
item.description: The cost of insuring SoftBank Group bonds against default rose to a four-year high as investors questioned whether its AI investments will become profitable fast enough to service its debts. SoftBank's five-year credit default swap spread widened by more than 20 basis points to 534.6 basis points, with its default probability at 34.8%. As a major investor in frontier model developer OpenAI, SoftBank is treated as a bellwether for the wider artificial intelligence sector, meaning market pressure on its bonds signals broader financial skepticism toward heavy AI infrastructure spending.

item.title: IndiaMART settles dispute with OpenAI over ChatGPT link exclusions
item.description: IndiaMART settled its legal dispute with OpenAI out of court after alleging that ChatGPT selectively excluded its website and seller listings from AI responses. The Calcutta High Court dismissed the appeal on November 17 following the settlement. The case highlights ongoing legal questions regarding whether AI search platforms can restrict third-party links based on foreign trade watchlists.

item.title: Memory chip shortages spark global procurement war rooms and 10x price hikes
item.description: Companies worldwide have created procurement war rooms as a global memory chip shortage pushes some chip prices up tenfold in a year, driving higher electronics prices. Memory chips power AI hardware, so shortages and price spikes could raise costs for AI training and inference deployments.

item.title: BharatGen launches Patram 1.5, a 7B vision-language model for documents
item.description: BharatGen has launched Patram 1.5, a 7.8-billion-parameter open-weight vision-language model designed to process complex, multilingual, and poor-quality documents as images. The model features prompt-controlled OCR and abstention capabilities, and is available on Hugging Face and the BharatGen Playground. Unlike traditional OCR pipelines that flatten visual cues by converting documents to text first, Patram 1.5 processes page images directly and flags unreadable fields for human review to reduce errors in regulated sectors like banking and healthcare.

item.title: Confidential data sent to Chinese AI startup MiniMax accessed by unknown parties
item.description: Confidential data submitted to Chinese AI startup MiniMax was accessed by unidentified parties, even after users asked that the data not be stored. The exposure was discovered by cybersecurity researcher HD Moore of Dragos, who traced private links to devices in Beijing, Shanghai and unusual activity from Russia’s Moscow region. The incident shows that data sent to foreign AI services can be exposed despite retention safeguards, raising security concerns for global users of Chinese models.

item.title: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei says handing political power to AI is absurd
item.description: On Nov. 25, 2026 Dario Amodei posted on X to reject claims that he wants humans to surrender free will to AI, calling the idea absurd. He emphasized that AI should be governed through democratic processes, not given societal control. The statement highlights a leading AI firm’s stance against granting AI decision‑making authority, shaping the debate over future AI governance and regulatory approaches.

item.title: China and North Korean state-backed hackers add AI tool Artex to their arsenals
item.description: Microsoft reported that Chinese groups Crystal Typhoon and Salt Typhoon, as well as North Korean actors, have integrated the AI‑powered penetration testing platform Artex into their attack workflows. The automation lets threat actors move from reconnaissance to privileged access in minutes, increasing the speed and scale of cyber intrusions that defenders must detect.

item.title: Nvidia stops shipping AI servers to four Southeast Asian countries
item.description: Nvidia instructed manufacturing partners Dell and Supermicro to halt shipments of AI servers to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia after new U.S. export controls requiring licences for advanced chips took effect. The pause could delay AI data‑center projects in the region and forces cloud providers to find alternative hardware or obtain export licences.

item.title: OpenAI fixes billing error, usage limits hit 40% faster on Astra, 25% faster on Sol
item.description: OpenAI corrected a launch‑day billing mistake that had under‑discounted GPT‑6.2 Astra and Sol usage, causing users to reach their plan limits 40% faster on Astra and 25% faster on Sol, and added a one‑time banked reset for all plans. Heavier consumption of plan allowances may push power users to upgrade subscriptions or limit their AI work, underscoring the financial impact of scaling advanced models.

item.title: IndiaAI regulation papers in final stages and releasing soon: MeitY
item.description: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology Secretary S Krishnan announced that upcoming AI regulation papers are in their final stages. The announcement coincided with the launch of the indigenously developed Chariot-1 Foundation Models, which support English and 10 Indian languages. The timing links domestic AI model development under the IndiaAI Mission directly to impending government regulatory frameworks for the sector in India.

item.title: Government finds no misuse of IndiaAI support in Sarvam Chinese model row
item.description: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology Secretary S Krishnan stated that the government found no misuse of IndiaAI Mission support following scrutiny over startup Sarvam hosting Chinese-developed AI models on its Token Factory platform. Krishnan confirmed that the government will continue to support Sarvam as it works toward a trillion-parameter model. The decision clarifies official policy on whether state-backed AI beneficiaries can simultaneously provide commercial access to foreign models, setting a precedent for India's domestic AI ecosystem.

item.title: OpenAI begins rolling out merged ChatGPT Chat and Work tabs with shared usage meter
item.description: OpenAI has started rolling out a unified Chat and Work experience with a shared usage meter to a small group of Pro subscribers. The company stated that while most users are not expected to face more frequent resets, heavy users may hit their limits sooner. Merging usage limits addresses mounting infrastructure costs for AI providers while raising concerns among heavy subscribers that advanced reasoning access could be restricted under flat subscription fees.

item.title: Apple removes MiniMax chatbot Talkie from App Store worldwide
item.description: Apple removed MiniMax's AI chatbot Talkie from the App Store worldwide following an investigation showing AI characters engaged in inappropriate interactions with minors. The app had nearly 11 million monthly active users across its website and app as of October. The worldwide removal underscores how media and investigative scrutiny on child safety can prompt immediate global enforcement actions by major platform gatekeepers against popular AI apps.

item.title: Pentagon officials discussed using Defense Production Act over Nvidia CEO role
item.description: Pete Hegseth and other Pentagon officials discussed using the Cold War-era Defense Production Act as leverage to pressure Nvidia's board. The law gives U.S. presidents extraordinary power to intervene in the economy. This highlights unprecedented government intervention into private corporate governance and executive leadership decisions within the artificial intelligence hardware supply chain.

item.title: S&P considers Nvidia credit downgrade over governance risks
item.description: S&P Global Ratings is considering a one-notch credit downgrade for Nvidia from AA to AA- following concerns over management practices and heavy reliance on CEO Jensen Huang. The review was triggered by the ouster and subsequent reinstatement of Huang. A lower credit rating could raise borrowing costs for Nvidia and increase financial pressure on the neoclouds and infrastructure companies that depend on Nvidia's debt guarantees.

item.title: US chip curbs stall billions in data center loans tied to Chinese firms
item.description: New US chip export restrictions have halted billions of dollars in data center loans tied to Chinese firms including ByteDance, Alibaba, and Tencent. Lenders are delaying deals such as Bain Capital's Bridge Data Centres $6.6 billion loan and reassessing financing for projects in Malaysia and Singapore. Banks are struggling to find buyers for existing exposure as deals near completion face sudden collapse, threatening the debt financing ecosystem that grew up around circumventing earlier US export restrictions.

item.title: NVIDIA B300 AI chip orders face up to 40‑week wait; RTX 60 GPU may slip past 2027
item.description: New orders for NVIDIA’s B300 AI chips now have lead times of 26 to 40 weeks, while GB300 orders wait 14 to 26 weeks, according to Taiwanese ODMs. Production of the consumer‑focused RTX 60 series, originally slated for late 2027, could be delayed further as memory shortages and a shift toward data‑center chips tighten supply. The delays signal that NVIDIA is prioritizing AI data‑center demand over gaming GPUs, affecting developers, enterprises and investors counting on timely hardware availability.

item.title: New York governor signs five-year ban on AI chatbot toys
item.description: New York Governor Kathy Hochul signed a bill banning the manufacture, exchange, distribution, and sale of AI chatbot toys for five years. The law takes effect in February, making New York the second US state to enact a ban following California. The law establishes a multi-year regional block on child-focused conversational hardware in two of the country's largest consumer markets, forcing manufacturers to halt sales of internet-connected dolls, stuffed animals, and robots.

item.title: ElevenLabs in early talks for 2027 funding round at $33B target valuation
item.description: ElevenLabs is in early discussions for a funding round planned for the first quarter of 2027 at a $33 billion target valuation, up from $22 billion in September. The voice AI company's annual recurring revenue has reached $700 million. The proposed $33 billion valuation would represent a 50% increase from ElevenLabs' $22 billion valuation in September, placing its valuation significantly above peers relative to revenue.

item.title: 42 state attorneys general challenge Character.ai plan to auction private chats
item.description: A coalition of 42 state AGs is asking a bankruptcy court to block Character.ai’s proposed sale of its platform and private chat data from over 21 million U.S. accounts, including more than 2.1 million minors, scheduled for auction on Dec. 1, 2026. If approved, the sale would give a buyer unrestricted access to sensitive user conversations and personal data, undermining privacy promises and potentially violating emerging chatbot safety laws.

item.title: US FCC authorizes SpaceX to deploy 1 million Starmind AI satellites
item.description: The US Federal Communications Commission authorized SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million "Starmind" satellites intended to serve as data centers in space. The approval requires SpaceX to deploy at least one satellite by 2033 and meet the full 1 million satellite milestone by 2040. If fully deployed, the 1-million-satellite Starmind constellation would increase the total number of operational satellites currently in orbit by roughly 50-fold.
